newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP fails to capture majority in Japan election.
newsitem.headline: LDP fails to capture majority in Japan election.

text.p: The Liberal Democratic Party of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto failed to win an outright majority in Japan's general election on Sunday, television network projections showed.

With only eight seats still undecided, the LDP had won 238 as of 12.30 a.m. on Monday (1530 GMT Sunday), making it impossible to win an overall majority of 251, according to projections by NHK public television based on returns.
Hashimoto had conceded earlier that his party would need to find coalition parties in order to remain in power.
The LDP was the dominant partner in the outgoing coalition government, which included the Social Democratic Party and Sakigake, an LDP splinter group.
Despite its failure to win an overall majority, the LDP had improved its performance from the 211 seats it previously held and remains by far the largest political party in Japan.
Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) was expected to come in second by winning about 155 seats in the new 500-member Lower House, down from 160 in the old House, which had 511 seats.
